examShortTricks: Trick 1: Dehydration: C2H5OH —(conc. H2SO4, 170 °C)→ C2H4 + H2O; dehydrohalogenation: C2H5Br + KOH(alcoholic) → C2H4 + KBr + H2O — 'alcoholic KOH' vs 'aqueous KOH' decides alkene vs alcohol.
Trick 2: Saytzeff rule for the 2-mark extra: elimination removes H from the β-carbon with FEWER hydrogens → more substituted (stable) alkene predominates.
Trick 3: Partial hydrogenation: RC≡CR + H2 (Lindlar/Pd–BaSO4) → cis-alkene; full reduction gives alkane.
